newsitem.title: USA: Broward Cty, Fla., sees $2 bln building boom-paper.
newsitem.headline: Broward Cty, Fla., sees $2 bln building boom-paper.

text.p: The value of property in Florida's Broward County rose to $59.8 billion this year, an increase of $2 billion or 3.3 percent over last year, the Miami Herald said in its Broward edition Tuesday.
County Property Appraiser William Markham said the trend is a continuation of a building frenzy that began five years ago after Hurricane Andrew devastated portions of neighboring Dade County.
Markham also attributed the trend to the general economic health of the county, which encompasses the Fort Lauderdale area.
Pembroke Pines saw the biggest gain in property value for the year, $330 million, followed by Miramar, Davie, Coconut Creek and Parkland.
